cases.reason: The reader put '2002 standard arithmetic' in scope and dismissed it on the argument 'truncation toward zero cannot move a value across -1, so 32 vs 34 digits cannot change validity'. That holds for 2002's truncation, but the compiler at --std 2002 does not truncate argument-1 to 32 digits: it carries 34 digits and ROUNDS (the PB5575 cause), and rounding can carry a value across -1. 2002 evaluates an argument-1 expression under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD by 8.8.1.3 (sum truncated to 32 significant digits); the check of AR2 then raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION only for an 'incorrect value' (15.2). Probe pvb.cob at --std 2002 under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD with EC-ALL checking: PRESENT-VALUE((-1 + 1 / 10 ** 35) 10 ** -40) raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, and PRESENT-VALUE((-1 + 1 / 10 ** 33) 10 ** -40) raises nothing. In 2002 both arguments have the SAME value: -0.99999999999999999999999999999999 (32 nines, the exact sum truncated to 32 significant digits). So the compiler gives these two arguments different validity, which 2002 never does. Read either way the 2002 AR2 check reaches: compared with all 32 digits (8.8.1.3.1.1: rounded below 32 'only as explicitly specified'), both are > -1, and PV35's EC is wrong. Rounded to 31 digits as a comparison (8.8.1.3.1.3 situation 1), both are -1, invalid, and PV33's missing EC is wrong. Either way the 2002 AR2 behavior for an argument-1 expression under standard arithmetic is not what the 2023 row shows (the 2023 row's witnesses are data items PIC S9V9 and native arithmetic, and 2023 has no 2002 STANDARD mode: --std 2023 refuses ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, COBOL0807). The scope item 'argument-1 under 2002 standard arithmetic' has no evidence, and the compiler is wrong for it.

cases.reason: The format and argument rule are identical. SIN has no equivalent arithmetic expression, so under 2002 standard arithmetic its value is implementor-defined apart from what RV1 states (2002 15.3.1). RV1 requires only an approximation inside [-1, +1], and a 34-digit approximation (the compiler's) satisfies that. The 31-digit rounding of the argument (8.8.1.3.1.3 situation 2) and the 32-digit container (15.3.1) are other rules' requirements, not this one's. No communication-section or removed-form reach.

cases.reason: The text is identical apart from digit grouping, and so are the format and the argument rule. I attacked it with an argument that is an integer only under 2002 standard arithmetic: (20240229 + 1 / 10 ** 32) truncated to 32 digits is exactly 20240229. At --std 2002 under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD the compiler REFUSES this at compile time (COBOL1627, citing §2023:15.3 type 6), probe tdb.cob. That is a question for the INTEGER argument-type rule (§2002:15.2 type 5, 'an arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value'), whose 2002 reading under standard arithmetic is arguable, and not for this returned-value rule: for every argument the compiler accepts, the integer value is mapped to 0/1/2/3 the same way in both editions. The 15.2 type-5 row should be read with tdb.cob in hand.
